lessons.title: Adab in our live lessons
objectives: Say why we listen to each other
Practise good adab in a live lesson
Link adab to the value of Excellence (ihsan)

keywords.def: good manners and behaviour
treating others with care
to pay attention with your ears and eyes
doing your best because Allah sees you

starter: Bismillah. Show me a kind hand.
Name one thing you can do to be kind.

teach.heading: The Tarbiyyah Compass and adab
bullets: Our school values are called the Tarbiyyah Compass
teach.note: Introduce the Tarbiyyah Compass simply: Resilience, Eeman, Contentment, Integrity, Progress, Excellence. Today's focus is Excellence and adab. Ground rules: right to pass, no personal stories, kindness. Pupils may ask anonymous questions via the teacher's question box. If a pupil says anything that worries you, stay calm, do not promise secrecy and follow the Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy: tell the DSL the same day.

teach.heading: Adab in a live lesson
bullets: Put up your hand to speak
teach.note: Model each action. Misconception: adab is only for school; it is for everywhere.

teach.heading: Kind chat and talking
bullets: Mute until it is your turn
teach.note: Practise unmuting politely. Ask 'how does it feel when everyone talks at once?'

teach.heading: Doing our best
bullets: Try your best even when it is hard
Allah loves when we do our best
teach.note: Cite plainly: ihsan means to do things in the best way. Keep language simple.

practice: Why do we put up a hand?
independent: Show good adab for starting a lesson: salaam, look, listen.
Role-play asking the teacher a question.
exit: Make a poster with three adab rules.
Tell a grown-up one rule you will keep.
homework: Name one rule for live lessons.
lessons.send: Show your family your adab poster and teach them one rule.

lessons.title: Friends and solving problems kindly
objectives: Say what makes a good friend
Use words to solve a problem
Say sorry and forgive

keywords.def: someone who is kind and plays with you
something that is hard or not working
to find a way to fix a problem
to stop being cross with someone

starter: Say one kind sentence to a friend.
What do you do when you are cross?

teach.heading: Good friends
teach.note: Ask who plays with whom. Stress including everyone. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said the best of you are those best in character (Sahih al-Bukhari). Ground rules: right to pass, no personal stories, kindness. Pupils may ask anonymous questions via the teacher's question box. If a pupil says anything that worries you, stay calm, do not promise secrecy and follow the Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy: tell the DSL the same day.

teach.heading: Solving problems
bullets: Ask a grown-up if you need help
teach.note: Role-play an argument over a toy, using two name cards for the two sides. Model calm voice. Misconception: hitting or shouting solves problems.

teach.heading: Sorry and forgiveness
bullets: Sorry means I will try to do better
teach.note: Teach the phrase 'It's okay, I forgive you'. Keep it sincere; no forced apologies.

teach.heading: Kindness plan
teach.note: Children choose from a list: share, help, smile, say thank you.

practice: What can you say instead of shouting?
independent: Practise using words to solve a pretend problem.
Draw two speech bubbles showing what two friends could say to solve a problem.
exit: Draw a problem (such as a broken toy) and how to solve it kindly, using objects and speech bubbles.
Write or say one kind sentence.
homework: Give one way to solve a problem.
lessons.send: Do one kind act and tell the class about it.

lessons.title: My body belongs to me
objectives: Know that our bodies belong to us
Know private parts are private
Know to tell a trusted adult if something feels wrong

keywords.def: just for you, not for others to see or touch
all of you, from head to toe
a grown-up you can ask for help
not safe, giving you a worried feeling

teach.heading: My body is mine
teach.note: Use calm and simple language. Use proper words where needed. Parents have been told in advance via the Parent Portal. Do not ask children to describe any personal experiences. Ground rules: right to pass, no personal stories, kindness. Pupils may ask anonymous questions via the teacher's question box. If a pupil says anything that worries you, stay calm, do not promise secrecy and follow the Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy: tell the DSL the same day.

teach.heading: Private parts are private
bullets: The parts covered by underwear are private
No one should look at or touch them unless to keep us clean or healthy
Doctors or parents can help in safe ways
teach.note: Use only the minimum language needed. Give the rule: private means private. Link to modesty (haya) in Islam.

teach.heading: Safe and unsafe
teach.note: Ask them to show thumbs up or down for example situations (a hug from a parent versus a stranger asking to see a toy).

teach.heading: Tell a trusted adult
bullets: Go away and tell a grown-up
teach.note: Stress it is never the child's fault. Teach 'Say no, go, tell'. Secrets that make you feel unsafe must be told.

practice: Who can you tell if you feel unsafe?
independent: Practise saying 'no, go, tell' with a grown-up at home.
exit: Draw your five trusted people on your hand.
Tell a grown-up your 'no, go, tell' plan.
homework: Is it your fault if someone makes you feel unsafe?
What do you do if you feel unsafe?
lessons.send: Share your safe hand with a family member and talk about who you would tell.

lessons.title: Online safety: ask first, be kind
objectives: Know to ask before clicking or downloading
Know to be kind online
Know to tell a grown-up about worries

keywords.def: connected to the internet
check with a grown-up before you click
to press with a mouse or tap with a finger
hurtful or not caring

starter: Bismillah. What do we do if something worries us on a screen?

teach.heading: The online world
bullets: Many websites and games are safe
teach.note: Ask what children do online. Stay positive and calm. Ground rules: right to pass, no personal stories, kindness. Pupils may ask anonymous questions via the teacher's question box. If a pupil says anything that worries you, stay calm, do not promise secrecy and follow the Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy: tell the DSL the same day.

teach.heading: Ask first
bullets: Ask before you tell your name
teach.note: Practise a pop-up scenario. 'Win a prize' pop-ups are tricks. Misconception: if it is on a screen it must be safe.

teach.heading: Be kind online
bullets: Use kind words in games and chat
Tell a grown-up if someone is unkind
teach.note: Link to adab and kind friends. Write a kind message together.

teach.heading: Tell a grown-up
bullets: You will not be in trouble
teach.note: Repeat the safety message. Show a 'stop and tell' sign.

practice: What do we do before we click?
What do we do if someone is unkind online?
independent: Sort pictures into 'ask first' and 'safe to do'.
exit: Make a poster: 'Ask first, be kind, tell'.
Say your poster rules to a grown-up.
homework: What should you do before downloading?
Who can you tell if you feel worried?
lessons.send: Teach your family your online safety rules.

lessons.title: Keeping clean: hands and teeth
lessons.bigQuestion: Germs are too small to see. How do we know they are on our hands?
objectives: To understand why keeping our hands and teeth clean keeps us healthy
successCriteria: All: show the steps of handwashing on camera
Most: say two times we must wash our hands
Some: explain how germs spread and how the miswak and toothbrush help
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: cleanliness (taharah) as part of faith

keywords.def: tiny living things that can make us ill
keeping ourselves clean
a twig used to clean the teeth (مِسْوَاك)
well and strong

hook.text: Germs are too small to see. How do we know they are on our hands?
hook.a: We cannot see them, but we can wash them away with soap and water.

islamicLink.text: The Prophet ﷺ taught that cleanliness is half of faith (Muslim). He loved the miswak and said that if it were not hard on his people, he would have told them to use it before every prayer (al-Bukhari and Muslim).

starter.q: Show me: what do we say before we eat?
Show me: one way to be kind in our lesson.
starter.a: For example: listen, wait our turn, kind words.

starter.q: Is a fruit a healthy snack? Thumbs up or down.

teach.heading: What are germs?
bullets: They live on hands and in mouths
teach.note: Use the glitter idea: sprinkle a little glitter (or flour) on your hand, shake a toy, show it spread.

teach.heading: Wash your hands
teach.note: Do it slowly on camera at a sink or with a bowl. Count to 20 while rubbing.

teach.heading: Clean teeth
teach.note: Show a miswak and a toothbrush.

check.q: When must we wash our hands?
options: After playing a game on the sofa
check.why: Before eating (and after the toilet) stops germs getting into our mouths.

practice.q: Show me the handwashing steps with your hands (no water).
practice.a: Wet, soap, rub backs, fingers and thumbs, rinse, dry.
practice.model: Teacher mimes each step slowly and counts to 20 while rubbing.

practice.q: Say two times we wash our hands.
practice.a: Before eating and after the toilet (also after playing outside).

independent.q: Core: Go to a sink with a grown-up and wash your hands properly, counting to 20. Come back and give a thumbs up.
independent.model: Teacher shows where the soap goes on the backs of the hands.

independent.q: Extend: Draw a toothbrush and a miswak and colour them in (objects only).
independent.a: A labelled drawing of a toothbrush and a miswak.

exit.q: Germs are... A) tiny and can make us ill B) big and friendly C) only on toys
exit.a: A) tiny and can make us ill
options: Tiny and can make us ill

exit.q: Big question: how do we get germs off our hands?
exit.a: Wash with soap and water for 20 seconds.

lessons.homework: Brush your teeth twice a day this week and tick a chart (pupil PDF) with your grown-up.
lessons.send: SEND: picture cards for each handwashing step. EAL: wash, soap, germs with actions. Stretch: say why we wash for 20 seconds.

Soap, water, towel at home (a grown-up helps)
Toothbrush and a miswak to show
Teeth chart (pupil PDF)
A pinch of glitter or flour for the germs demonstration

lessons.title: Staying healthy: food, water, sleep and moving
lessons.bigQuestion: If your body was a car, what would its fuel be?
objectives: To understand that food, water, sleep and moving our bodies help us stay healthy
successCriteria: All: name one healthy food and one treat
Most: say why we need water and sleep
Some: set one small healthy goal for the week
lessons.smsc: Moral: looking after the body as an amanah

keywords.def: good for our body
a food we have only sometimes
rest our body needs every night
something we try to do

hook.text: If your body was a car, what would its fuel be?
hook.a: Healthy food and water; and sleep is like parking it to rest.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Eat and drink, but do not waste by excess' (al-A'raf 7:31). Our bodies are a trust (amanah) from Allah, so we look after them.

starter.q: Show me: how long do we rub our hands with soap?
Show me: what do we use to clean our teeth?
Thumbs up or down: germs can make us ill.

teach.heading: Food
bullets: Say Bismillah and eat with the right hand
teach.note: Sort the foods.

teach.heading: Water and sleep
bullets: Water helps us think and play
Bedtime after Isha, early to rise
teach.note: Children of this age need about 10 to 12 hours of sleep.

teach.heading: Moving
teach.note: Do a 30-second stretch together (no music).

check.why: Sweets are fine sometimes; fruit and vegetables are for every day.

practice.q: Show me: draw one healthy food on your whiteboard.
practice.a: For example: an apple, a carrot, a banana.
practice.model: Teacher draws a banana and says 'every day food'.

practice.q: Thumbs up or down: we need sleep to grow.

independent.q: Core: Draw your healthy plate: three foods for every day (pupil PDF).
independent.a: A plate with three healthy foods.
independent.model: Teacher draws the first food on the plate.

independent.q: Extend: Choose one goal: drink water with every meal, or a fruit every day. Tell the class.

exit.q: Our body needs... A) only sweets B) food, water, sleep and moving C) only sleep
exit.a: B) food, water, sleep and moving

exit.q: Big question: what is our body's fuel?

lessons.homework: Try your goal every day this week and show your grown-up.
lessons.send: SEND: real or picture food cards to sort. EAL: food words with pictures. Stretch: say why water helps us.

Food picture cards

lessons.title: Likes, dislikes and being special
lessons.bigQuestion: If everyone in the world liked exactly the same food, games and colours, would the world be better or more boring?
objectives: To understand that Allah made everyone different and that our differences help us know one another
successCriteria: All: say one thing I like and one I do not like
Most: say one way I am different from a friend
Some: say why being different is a good thing
lessons.smsc: Social: respecting that friends like different things

keywords.def: there is only one of you
not the same as anyone else
something that makes you happy
not the same

hook.text: If everyone in the world liked exactly the same food, games and colours, would the world be better or more boring?
hook.a: More boring! Allah made us different so we can learn from each other.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted.' (Al-Hujurat 49:13). Allah made us different on purpose, and the best of us is the one with the most taqwa.

starter.q: Which is a kind thing to say?
Who made us?
A trusted adult is ...

teach.heading: We are all different
bullets: Different faces? No: we talk about likes
teach.note: Keep to likes and talents; no drawing of people. Use objects: a ball, a book, an apple.

teach.heading: My likes and dislikes
teach.note: Children hold up objects from home they like.

teach.heading: Allah made us different
bullets: So we can know one another
teach.note: Read the meaning of 49:13 slowly. Taqwa: being careful to please Allah.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll; share the results and explain the right answer and why the others are wrong.

check.q: Why did Allah make people different (49:13)?
options: So we can know one another

practice.q: Finish the sentence: 'I am special because I ...'
practice.a: For example: 'I am special because I am good at helping.'
practice.model: I do: 'I am special because I am good at reading Arabic letters.'

independent.q: Pupil PDF: draw two things you like (objects, food or places, no people) and one thing you do not like. Show it to the camera.
independent.a: Two likes and one dislike drawn.
independent.model: The teacher draws a book and an apple (likes) and a rain cloud (dislike).

independent.q: Extend: say one thing you like that your friend does not.
independent.a: For example: 'I like carrots, but my friend does not.'

exit.q: Back to our ponder: If everyone in the world liked exactly the same food, games and colours, would the world be better or more boring?
exit.a: More boring! Allah made us different so we can learn from each other.

lessons.homework: Ask someone at home about one thing they like that you do not; tell the class next time.
lessons.send: SEND: picture cards and one step at a time; a grown-up may help. EAL: key words with pictures. Stretch: explain your idea to the class in a full sentence.

lessons.title: Proud, not showing off; and our worries
lessons.bigQuestion: You just learned a new surah! What is a good way to feel happy about it, and what is not?
objectives: To understand how to feel proud in a good way by saying alhamdulillah, and how to notice when we feel worried
successCriteria: All: say alhamdulillah when I do something well
Most: say the difference between proud and showing off
Some: name something that makes me worried and who I can tell
lessons.smsc: Moral: humility: thanking Allah instead of showing off

keywords.def: happy about something good you did
making others feel small to look big
all praise is for Allah
a scared or uneasy feeling inside

hook.text: You just learned a new surah! What is a good way to feel happy about it, and what is not?
hook.a: Say alhamdulillah and keep trying; do not make others feel small.

islamicLink.text: We say 'alhamdulillah' (all praise is for Allah) when something good happens, because every good thing comes from Allah. Al-Fatihah begins with these words (1:2).

starter.q: Allah made people different so we can ...
Which is a like?
A trusted adult is ...

teach.heading: Proud or showing off?
teach.note: Read each card; children show thumbs up or down.

teach.heading: What does worry feel like?
teach.note: Children point to where they feel worry (tummy, head).

teach.heading: What helps a worry
teach.note: Talk through each step.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll; share the results and explain the right answer and why the others are wrong.

check.q: You won a race. What is the best thing to say?
options: I'm better than all of you!
check.why: We thank Allah and stay kind to others.

practice.q: Your friend reads beautifully. What could you say to them?
practice.model: I do: 'MashaAllah, that was lovely reading!' We are happy for others too.

independent.q: Pupil PDF: draw a 'worry jar' and write or draw one small worry to put in it, then the name of a trusted adult (a word or a symbol, no faces).
independent.a: A worry jar with one worry and a trusted adult named.
independent.model: The teacher draws a jar and writes 'a new lesson'; trusted adult: Mum.

independent.q: Extend: say one thing you are proud of and say alhamdulillah.
independent.a: For example: 'I tidied my room, alhamdulillah.'

exit.q: When we feel worried we can ...
Back to our ponder: You just learned a new surah! What is a good way to feel happy about it, and what is not?
exit.a: Say alhamdulillah and keep trying; do not make others feel small.

lessons.homework: Tell a grown-up one thing you are proud of this week and say alhamdulillah together.
lessons.send: SEND: picture cards and one step at a time; a grown-up may help. EAL: key words with pictures. Stretch: explain your idea to the class in a full sentence.

lessons.title: Staying calm and standing up for myself, online too
lessons.bigQuestion: Someone keeps taking your pencil. What could you say that is kind but firm?
objectives: To understand how to stay calm and say 'no' kindly but firmly, and what to do if something online feels wrong
successCriteria: All: take three calm breaths
Most: say 'Stop, I don't like that' in a firm voice
Some: say the online rule: stop, say no, tell
lessons.smsc: Moral: self-control and asking for help

keywords.def: quiet and relaxed inside
doing the right thing even when it is hard
a word that means I do not agree
let a trusted adult know

hook.text: Someone keeps taking your pencil. What could you say that is kind but firm?
hook.a: 'Please stop, I don't like that. Please give it back.' If it keeps happening, tell an adult.

islamicLink.text: The Prophet ﷺ said the strong person is not the one who wins a fight, but the one who controls himself when angry (reported by al-Bukhari and Muslim).

starter.q: When we do well we say ...
A worry can be shared with ...
Calm breathing is ...

teach.heading: Calm first
bullets: Say 'A'udhu billah' if you feel angry
teach.note: Do three breaths together on camera.

teach.heading: Say it kindly but firmly
teach.note: Practise the voice together.

teach.heading: Online: stop, say no, tell
teach.note: Link to portal Year 1 lesson 4 (ask first, be kind).

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll; share the results and explain the right answer and why the others are wrong.

check.q: A game online asks for your home address. What do you do?
check.why: Never share personal information; stop and tell.

practice.q: Practise: say 'Stop, I don't like that' in a calm, firm voice.
practice.a: Children say it clearly with a calm face.
practice.model: I do: I stand tall, breathe, and say clearly: 'Stop, I don't like that.'

independent.q: Pupil PDF: draw a traffic light; next to red write 'stop', amber 'say no', green 'tell'.
independent.a: A traffic light with the three steps.
independent.model: The teacher draws the red light and writes 'stop'.

independent.q: Extend: name two trusted adults, one at home and one at TGA.
independent.a: For example: Dad and my class teacher.

exit.q: If something online feels wrong we ...
Back to our ponder: Someone keeps taking your pencil. What could you say that is kind but firm?
exit.a: 'Please stop, I don't like that. Please give it back.' If it keeps happening, tell an adult.

lessons.homework: Show a grown-up your traffic light and practise calm breathing together.
lessons.send: SEND: picture cards and one step at a time; a grown-up may help. EAL: key words with pictures. Stretch: explain your idea to the class in a full sentence.

successCriteria: All: name two trusted adults
Most: say what to say when I need help

what someone gives when you need it
a feeling that something might go wrong

hook.text: If you got lost in a big shop, who would you ask for help?
hook.a: A trusted adult: the person at the till or a family with children, and stay where you are.

islamicLink.text: Allah loves people who help each other. Allah says: 'And cooperate in righteousness and piety' (Al-Ma'idah 5:2).

starter.q: Which is kind?
When we start a lesson we ...
Say one thing that makes you happy.
starter.a: For example: playing with my sister.

teach.heading: My helpers
bullets: A grandparent or older family member
teach.note: Children hold up fingers for each helper they can name.

teach.heading: How to ask
teach.note: Practise the words together.
cycle: If they don't help, ask another

teach.heading: Helper or not?
teach.note: Children point to the right side.

cards: Someone I don't know in the park

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll; share the results and explain the right answer and why the others are wrong.

check.q: You fall and hurt your knee. Who do you tell?

lessons.title: Proud and jealous: feelings we notice

a feeling of wanting what someone else has
words we say when we like something Allah gave someone

starter.q: A trusted adult is ...
To ask for help we say ...
Show a happy face with your hands.

teach.heading: Jealous

lessons.unit: Summer 2: Joining in and joining up
lessons.title: Listening well, giving my opinion and knowing right from wrong
lessons.bigQuestion: Is it better to have ice cream or fruit for pudding? Think of a reason!
objectives: To understand how to listen to others, share my opinion kindly and tell right from wrong
successCriteria: All: show good listening with my eyes, ears and mouth
Most: give my opinion with 'I think ... because ...'
Some: say why a choice is right or wrong

keywords.def: to pay attention to what someone says
what you think about something
telling the truth

hook.text: Is it better to have ice cream or fruit for pudding? Think of a reason!
hook.a: Any answer with a reason: an opinion is what you think, and a reason says why.

islamicLink.text: The Prophet ﷺ listened carefully to people and spoke kindly. Allah loves truthfulness: being honest is always right.

starter.q: A trusted adult is ...
When I feel jealous I can say ...
Show a thumbs up if you are ready to listen.

teach.heading: Good listening
bullets: Mouth closed until it's my turn
teach.note: Children show each one.

teach.heading: My opinion
teach.note: Practise the sentence together.

teach.heading: Right or wrong?
teach.note: Children point to the side.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll; share the results and explain the right answer and why the others are wrong.

check.q: You broke a cup by accident. What is right?

practice.a: For example: 'I like rain because I can jump in puddles.'
practice.model: I do: 'I like reading because I learn new words.'

independent.q: Pupil PDF: circle the right choices in four pictures of objects (a returned pencil case, a shared box of crayons, a broken toy hidden in a bin, a tidy room), then say one opinion to the class.
independent.a: Right: returned pencil case, shared crayons, tidy room. Wrong: hiding the broken toy.
independent.model: The teacher circles the returned pencil case: 'giving back what isn't mine is right'.

independent.q: Extend: tell a grown-up one thing that is right and why.

exit.q: 'I think ... because ...' is how we give ...
Back to our ponder: Is it better to have ice cream or fruit for pudding? Think of a reason!
exit.a: Any answer with a reason: an opinion is what you think, and a reason says why.

lessons.homework: At dinner, ask everyone their opinion about a favourite fruit and listen to each answer.
lessons.send: SEND: picture cards and one step at a time; a grown-up may help. EAL: key words with pictures. Stretch: explain your idea to the class in a full sentence.

lessons.unit: Summer 2: Joining in and joining up
lessons.title: Caring for living things: animals and plants need us
lessons.bigQuestion: A bird lands on your window sill on a very hot day. What might it need?
objectives: To understand what animals and plants need and how we can care for them kindly
successCriteria: All: name three things an animal needs
Most: say who looks after animals (vets, farmers, owners)
Some: explain why being kind to animals pleases Allah
lessons.crossCurricular: Science: what animals and plants need to live

keywords.def: things a living thing must have to stay alive and well
looking after something kindly
mercy and kindness (رحمة)

hook.text: A bird lands on your window sill on a very hot day. What might it need?
hook.a: Water and shade: animals need food, water, shelter and kindness.

islamicLink.text: The Prophet ﷺ told of a man who gave water to a very thirsty dog, and Allah forgave him because of it (al-Bukhari and Muslim). Being kind to animals is loved by Allah.

starter.q: An opinion is ...
Telling the truth is ...
Name an animal you like.

teach.heading: What animals need
teach.note: Children hold up a finger for each need.

teach.heading: Who looks after animals?
teach.note: Match the helper to the job.

head: Helper
What they do
rows: Gives food, water and a clean home

teach.heading: Plants need us too
teach.note: Link to science: a plant on the windowsill.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll; share the results and explain the right answer and why the others are wrong.

options: food, water and a safe home
check.why: All animals need food, water and shelter.

practice.q: Say one way to be kind to a garden bird.
practice.model: I do: 'I can put a dish of water outside on a hot day.'

independent.q: Pupil PDF: draw lines from each animal (cat, bird, fish, rabbit) to what it needs, then colour the plant picture and draw its water and sun.
independent.a: Each animal matched to food, water and shelter; plant with water and sun drawn.
independent.model: The teacher matches the fish to clean water.

independent.q: Extend: with a grown-up, give water to a plant or put out water for birds.

exit.q: Being kind to animals is called ...
Back to our ponder: A bird lands on your window sill on a very hot day. What might it need?
exit.a: Water and shade: animals need food, water, shelter and kindness.

lessons.homework: With a grown-up, care for a living thing this week: water a plant or put out water for birds.
lessons.send: SEND: picture cards and one step at a time; a grown-up may help. EAL: key words with pictures. Stretch: explain your idea to the class in a full sentence.
